title: Permission architecture: the unverified controls and the self-modification exposure

completion_criteria.text: Establish whether the R3 bypassPermissions precondition is enforced or is prose only - nothing enforcing it means the mode is reachable today, which is what makes the deny question load-bearing
Measured with evidence: whether a permissions.deny rule and a PreToolUse deny both hold under bypassPermissions, with the SPEC's claim at line 274 marked verified or refuted
Measured with a paired control: which decision wins when allow-write-tools.sh and secret-scanner.sh both fire on one Edit, and the secret deny confirmed to hold or the registration fixed so it does
A recorded decision on the self-modification exposure: accept it as the price of unattended autonomy, or ship a report that surfaces a changed gate or settings file after the fact
If that decision calls for machinery it ships and is proven: the report fires on a real gate edit, stays silent otherwise, and never blocks, since prevention was deliberately removed

spine.active_goal: Close the two unverified controls left by the permission rebuild, and rule on the self-modification exposure it deliberately created.
spine.next_step: START HERE. spine.last_session: Opened as the successor to max-autonomy-permission-build, carrying the three risks the owner selected at its close. No work done on it yet.

open_risks.text: Measure whether a deny rule survives bypassPermissions before trusting any unattended run — deny is the only control left on the PR-creation, PR-merge and hosted-Supabase surfaces, and no experiment has ever covered that mode

Measure which decision wins when allow-write-tools.sh and secret-scanner.sh both fire on one Edit — deny beating allow is inference, and if it is wrong the secret scanner is silently dead on every write

An agent can rewrite or delete the gate that judges it in one unattended command — G4 is retired in full so every guardrail-file write allows; git is the only recovery and nothing reports the change until a human looks

out_of_scope: The logbook fail-closed PreToolUse guard - it belongs to the logbook plugin repository rather than this one, per its decision record
Reinstating any G4 guardrail-write control - two decision records retired it, and c4 rules on detection after the fact, never on prevention
